C-73.IntentSummary: Land the three-layer regression baseline: static advertised-chord routing audit, behavioral affordance-audit e2e (chords, menu-bridge walk, welcome actions), and the 2.5.x manual checklist with a train-freeze execution protocol; record the FIX-012 finding the walk surfaced.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Seven assertions over registry/menu/front-menu advertised chords versus native/keydown/zoom routes, with collision detection, per-id agreement and the UC-025 ⇧⌘P reservation; population guards fail on extractor drift. Green on current main.

Real-key chord sweep with generic response detection plus markdown-anchored duplicate/heading cases; menu-bridge walk over all registry leaves with reasoned allowlists and zero unexpected warnings; welcome action responses; FIX-009 fixme case visible. Known-open FIX-012 recorded with the walk as its reproducer.
regression-tests.json covers the 2.5.x surface with the train-freeze executionProtocol; V-M-009 scenario-17 and V-M-012 scenario-71 recorded; FIX-012 train record written; grace lint clean.

Corner.Name: Correctness
Corner.Expected: Extractors parse real current shapes: registry arrays (23 shortcuts), m009 taxonomy struct literals AND builder .accelerator chains, /^Digit([1-6])$/ class, zoom '='+'+' alias. Empty-extraction populations fail loudly. Walk asserts bridge listener presence per id.

Corner.Name: Correctness — false confidence
Corner.Expected: Allowlists are exhaustive-with-reasons, not blankets: NO_RESPONSE_ALLOWLIST covers native-dialog and capability-gated commands only; EXPECTED_BRIDGE_WARNINGS covers help.rate and FIX-012 only; any new entry fails. fixme is limited to the FIX-009 case.

Corner.Name: Stability
Corner.Expected: Response detection accepts any of bus/DOM/invoke/state-digest so the sweep does not over-pin implementations; welcome clicks ordered so the navigating action (New) runs last; walk gaps (50ms) keep renders settleable. No reliance on minified names.

Corner.Name: Security
Corner.Expected: Test-only payloads: synthetic documents, no owner content, no paths outside the repo and /tmp/mark-e2e. No secrets; public-repo hygiene unchanged.

Corner.Name: UX
Corner.Expected: The audit encodes the user contract "what the UI advertises must work" — chords, menu items and buttons. The FIX-009 fixme keeps a known dead affordance visible instead of hidden.

Corner.Name: Performance
Corner.Expected: Static test ~1.5s; e2e spec ~17s in Chromium (within existing suite budget); no runtime code touched.

Corner.Name: Verification honesty
Corner.Expected: Every scenario text names its files and its known-open exceptions; the FIX-012 record separates "found by automation" from owner reports and does not claim acceptance.

Corner.Name: Concurrency
Corner.Expected: Parallel-session work respected: FIX-011 (untitled dialog) numbering kept; this change's finding renumbered to FIX-012; shared docs edited additively.

Corner.Name: Maintainability
Corner.Expected: New chord sources or routes extend one extractor each; RESERVED_CHORDS/ROUTED_ELSEWHERE tables document every exemption with an owner and reason.

Corner.Name: Delivery
Corner.Expected: No release action: nothing queued, tagged or published. The checklist protocol references train freeze but authorizes nothing by itself.

Review.note: Extractor bugs found and fixed during development (Rust .to_string() suffix, Digit character class, '+' alias); final state 7/7 green with population guards verified non-vacuous.
Walk reproduced FIX-012 deterministically across runs; isolated pairs clean — documented as state-dependent; response polling capped at 2.5s.
Synthetic fixtures only; no owner data; no signing material.
FIX-009 fixme and FIX-012 record keep known dead affordances visible; no user-facing behavior changed.
